digest.component_or_area: LLM runtime provider abstraction and model selection
propositions: rebar's LLM runtime is hardcoded for Anthropic providers with conditional branches on provider strings (runner.py:268, runner.py:316, structured.py:46) instead of using an extensible seam, blocking first-class support for AWS Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Documentation claims REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY are functional (docs/llm-framework.md:126-133,226) but the runtime refuses them in _pai_check_config (runner.py:653), making the documentation false.

AWS Bedrock-hosted Anthropic Claude is inaccessible as a first-class provider; the only path is fronting Bedrock with an OpenAI gateway, which loses prompt caching, retrying transport, per-request timeout, native structured output, and accurate model provenance in signed verdicts.
Signed verdict sidecars record a model string that no longer names the actual provider when using gateway wrappers, making provenance opaque to consumers.

Bedrock retry and timeout configuration (llm_retry_max_attempts, llm_retry_max_wait_s, timeout_s) do not reach the botocore client; only the direct-Anthropic path has tenacity envelope and httpx timeout, leaving the live production Bedrock path unconfigured.
